result.summary: Removes redundant assertions verifying WALLET_FLAG_DESCRIPTORS across several descriptor-specific CWallet methods. It also moves the descriptor flag check out of UpgradeDescriptorCache() into its callers (CWallet::Unlock and WalletBatch::LoadWallet).
result.problem: Because legacy wallets can no longer be loaded for normal operations, multiple assertions checking for descriptor wallets are obsolete or redundant in descriptor-specific methods, adding cognitive overhead for developers. In addition, checking the descriptor flag inside UpgradeDescriptorCache() obscured the fact that its callers can still handle legacy wallets in migration workflows.
evidence: PR description: "Since the legacy wallet can't be loaded anymore, few of these assertions are outdated now. Seeing too many of these assertions in the CWallet class while reading the code is cognitively loaded"

Commit 77778e2559: "The UpgradeDescriptorCache method ends up being called via the CWallet::Unlock and WalletBatch::LoadWallet methods, both of which can be called for the legacy wallets within the context of wallet migration... This move out of the check makes it explicit for the reader that this is not the only flow for these callers."
result.changed_since_previous: No changes to the patch; previous description was recorded when the diff was not yet populated.
result.card: Removes redundant assertions verifying WALLET_FLAG_DESCRIPTORS across descriptor-specific CWallet methods and moves the descriptor check in UpgradeDescriptorCache() up to its callers. The author notes that because legacy wallets can no longer be loaded normally, internal descriptor assertions are largely obsolete and add cognitive overhead. Furthermore, moving the check to callers like CWallet::Unlock clarifies code paths that still handle legacy wallets during migration. This is an internal wallet cleanup with no user-facing behavioral changes.

risk.why: Mistakes could cause an assertion failure or execute descriptor upgrade logic on a legacy wallet during migration.
